trailheadDirection: From the Verlot Public Service Center on the Mountain Loop Highway, continue east about 4.6 miles and turn right onto Forest Road 4020 (Schweitzer Creek Road, signed for Boardman Lake/Ashland Lakes/Bear-Pinnacle Lake).

trailhead: Pinnacle Peak Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive Paradise Road about 15 miles to the Stevens Canyon Road junction, turn right and go 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking area; the trailhead is on the south side of the road.

trailhead: Pinnacle Saddle Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Pinnacle Saddle Trailhead across Stevens Canyon Road from the Reflection Lakes parking (~4,860 ft); when the road is snow-gated, winter parties start from the Narada Falls pullout

trailhead: Pinnacle Saddle Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
trailheadDirection: Park at the Reflection Lakes pullouts on Stevens Canyon Road (1.4 miles east of the Paradise-Longmire Road junction, roughly 1.9 miles from the Paradise turnoff).

trailhead: Pond pullout east of Washington Pass (SR-20)
trailheadDirection: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington/Sedro-Woolley, then east on SR-20 through Marblemount and over Rainy Pass to Washington Pass; from Winthrop/Mazama it's a quick 20-30 minute drive west on SR-20 instead.

The standard-route trailhead is the Putvin Trailhead (Trail #813) on Hamma Hamma Road (FR-25), about 11.8-12.1 miles west of Hwy 101 and about 4.5 miles past the Lena Lake trailhead, at roughly 1,600 ft elevation.
From the Pyramid Lake Trailhead on SR-20 (6.4 miles past Newhalem; parking pullout on the left, ~6 cars, trail on the right side of the highway)
From the Pyramid Lake Trailhead on SR-20 (6.4 miles past Newhalem)
From the Rachel Lake Trailhead (2,800 ft, end of FS Rd 4930 off Kachess Lake Rd, Exit 62 from I-90), start on Rachel Lake Trail #1313.
Start at the Rachel Lake Trailhead (Trail #1313, elev. ~2,800 ft) at the end of Box Canyon Road/FR-4930.

trailhead: Rainy Pass / Lake Ann–Maple Pass Trailhead
trailheadDirection: From the paved pullout at Rainy Pass (4,855 ft) on SR-20 — signed 'Rainy Pass Trailhead,' 52 miles east of Marblemount, right where the PCT crosses the highway — start on the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail (well-graded, heavily used).
From the PCT North trailhead parking at Rainy Pass on SR-20 (~4,860 ft)

From the Reynolds Creek Trailhead (~3,100-3,170 ft, reached via Forest Road 4435, which crosses the Twisp River near Mystery Campground before the Spur 4435-015 turnoff to the trailhead), the route follows Reynolds Creek Trail #402, an unmaintained, primitive Forest Service trail entering the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
From the roadside pullout

trailhead: Robinson Creek Trailhead (Lost River Road / Forest Road 5400)
trailheadDirection: From the Robinson Creek Trailhead off Lost River Road/Forest Road 5400 past Mazama

trailhead: Robinson Creek Trailhead (Lost River Road / FR 5400)
trailheadDirection: From Winthrop drive about 15 miles west on SR 20, turn right onto Lost River Road, keep left after half a mile, and follow it about 7.5 miles on pavement, then 1.25 miles on gravel FR 5400 to the Robinson Creek Trailhead on the right.

From the Rock Mountain Trail #1587 pullout on US-2 (small dirt lot on the north side of the highway near the powerlines, no facilities), the trail launches immediately uphill on what was formerly a service road.
From the Ross Dam Trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 134, down to Ross Lake and the water-taxi/trail network
From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east about 14 miles; the trailhead parking is on the right between mileposts 134 and 135.
From the Ross Dam Trailhead at Happy Flats on SR 20 (~milepost 134, 2,150 ft), it's about 1 mile down to the Ross Lake water taxi dock; cross the lake by taxi (or paddle) to Big Beaver Landing.
From Leavenworth, drive US Highway 2 west approximately 17.4-17.7 miles (or from Stevens Pass, drive east about 18 miles) to just past the Nason Creek Rest Area.

Drive Hwy 101 to just before Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Rd, then Palo Alto Rd (becomes FR 28) for about 6 miles, turn right on FR 2880 along the Dungeness River, then in 1.7 miles turn left on FR 2870 and continue roughly 6.5-9 miles (gravel, winds steeply down to a river crossing) to the large Dungeness/Royal Basin trailhead lot (picnic table, vault toilet).

trailhead: Ruth Creek Road pullout near milepost 3 (FS 32)
trailheadDirection: From a pullout near milepost 3 on Ruth Creek Road, just past a creek flowing over a concrete weir (~2,950 ft), off Hannegan Pass Road (FS 32) from the Mt. Baker Highway
From Twisp, drive Twisp River Road west approximately 22-24 miles to the Scatter Creek/Scatter Lake trailhead (~3,100-3,200 ft), about 50 yards past the Slate Creek Trail junction sign.
From the Schriebers Meadow / Park Butte Trailhead (~3,360 ft) south of Mount Baker, via the Scott Paul Trail #603.1
From the Schriebers Meadow / Park Butte Trailhead (~3,360 ft) south of Mount Baker
From the Shannon Ridge Trailhead at the end of FR-1152-014 (~2,500 ft) off Baker Lake Road
From the pullout where SR-20 crosses Silver Star Creek near milepost 171 (~3,450 ft), about 8.5 miles east of Washington Pass

From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37).

From the Stevens Pass Ski Area's north (uphill) lot, walk to the far east end of the parking area near the small gray electrical substation/WSDOT building — this is the unsigned Skyline Lake trailhead.

Park in the large day-use lot on the north side of US 2 right at the Stevens Pass summit (signed for the PCT/Skyline Lake trailhead); a Northwest Forest Pass or Forest Service day-use fee applies here.

From the Slate Pass trailhead (~6,900', reached via the Harts Pass Road — one of the highest drivable roads in Washington), pick up the Buckskin Ridge Trail #498 heading north/northeast into the Pasayten Wilderness.

From Mazama, take Lost River Road, which becomes FR-5400 where the pavement ends, and follow the gravel road to Harts Pass; the Slate Pass trailhead is at the second switchback on the road beyond Harts Pass.

From Mazama take Lost River Road, which becomes Harts Pass Road (FR 5400), to Harts Pass; at the guard station turn right onto Slate Peak Road (FR 5400-600) and climb to the Slate Pass Trailhead at the second switchback beyond the horse loading area, about 6,900 ft. High clearance recommended.

trailhead: Slate Pass Trailhead (Harts Pass Road FR-5400)
trailheadDirection: From Slate Pass (~6,900 ft) at the end of Harts Pass Road
Park at the Smithbrook Trailhead (elev. ~4,000 ft) on Smithbrook Road (FR 6700), about 3 miles up from Hwy 2.

From US Highway 2 about 4 miles east of Stevens Pass, turn onto Smith Brook Road (Forest Road 6700) and follow the gravel road roughly 2.6-2.8 miles to the Smithbrook Trailhead (el. ~4,000 ft; no fee, no Northwest Forest Pass required). The road is closed to vehicles under a storm-damage order effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless lifted sooner; confirm it has reopened before driving.

Drive US 2 to Smithbrook Road (Forest Road 6700); the turnoff is about 4.2 miles east of Stevens Pass summit (roughly half a mile east of milepost 69 coming from the Leavenworth/Wenatchee side, or about 68 miles from Everett/Seattle).

trailhead: Snow Lake Trailhead (Stevens Canyon Road, Mount Rainier NP)
trailheadDirection: From the Snow Lake Trailhead on Stevens Canyon Road (~4,500 ft); Stevens Canyon Road closes in winter — winter parties typically start from Narada Falls
Start at the Snow Lakes Trailhead (paved, day-use permit required, ~4 miles up Icicle Creek Road from Leavenworth).
From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Road (Forest Road 7600) about 4.2–4.3 miles west to the Snow Lakes Trailhead and parking area on the south side of the road (~1,350 ft).
From the Snow Lakes Trailhead on Icicle Creek Road (about 4.2 mi from US-2, ~1,300 ft elevation)

Drive to the Berry Patch or Snowgrass Flat Trailhead (Chambers Lake area) off Forest Road 21/2150 on the west side of the Goat Rocks: turn east onto FR 21, continue about 13 miles, turn at the Snowgrass Trail/Chambers Lake sign onto FR 2150, then follow signs to the Snowgrass Flat Trailhead (elev. ~4,650 ft).
From the Snowgrass Flats Trailhead (end of FR-2150, elev. ~4,600 ft), start on Trail 96 (Snowgrass Flat Trail).
Start at the Snowgrass Trailhead (elev. ~4,650 ft), reached via FR-21 (Johnson Creek Road) off US-12 about 3 miles west of Packwood.

trailhead: Sol Duc Trailhead (end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Road)
trailheadDirection: From US-101 about 28 miles west of Port Angeles, turn onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road and follow it about 13.8 miles, past the park entrance station and the resort, to the road end and trailhead parking.
From the Sol Duc Trailhead at the end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Road

From US-101 about 28 miles west of Port Angeles, turn onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road and follow it about 13.8 miles, past the park entrance station and the resort, to the road end and trailhead parking.
